Use it for\\\\n  alarms on AWS/EBS metrics (VolumeReadOps, VolumeWriteOps, VolumeReadBytes,\\\\n  VolumeWriteBytes, VolumeQueueLength, VolumeTotalReadTime/WriteTime,\\\\n  VolumeAvgReadLatency, VolumeStalledIOCheck, BurstBalance) or\\\\n  EBSIOBalance%/EBSByteBalance%; for sizing\\\\n  IOPS or throughput changes; for requests to raise IOPS or modify a volume; for a\\\\n  volume modification that looks stuck or failed; for deciding which snapshots or\\\\n  AMIs need owner review before deletion, or how to recover them; for KMS errors\\\\n  on encrypted volumes; for EBS quota or limit errors; for a jump in the EBS bill;\\\\n  and for a pre-launch EBS review. Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx, instance store,\\\\n  or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Troubleshoot Amazon EBS performance, volume modifications, snapshots, encryption, quotas and cost, and review an account\\'s EBS setup with read-only checks.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes. Troubleshoot mode answers \\\\\"something is wrong, why?\\\\\" through one of five paths and returns a fixed verdict. Review mode answers \\\\\"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\\\\\" and returns a rated report. Both modes are read-only and share the same volume-type rules, instance limits and service rules. Load only the reference files the request needs.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use This Skill\\\\n\\\\n- Storage-related slowness, timeouts or high I/O latency on an Amazon EC2 instance.\\\\n- An alarm on AWS/EBS metrics or on instance `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%`.\\\\n- A request to raise IOPS or throughput, or to modify a volume.\\\\n- A volume modification that looks stuck, failed, or did not improve performance.\\\\n- Snapshot, AMI, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, AWS Backup or Recycle Bin questions, including which snapshots need owner review before deletion.\\\\n- Encrypted-volume access errors and AWS KMS questions for Amazon EBS.\\\\n- Amazon EBS cost increases, idle or over-provisioned volumes.\\\\n- An operation that failed on an Amazon EBS quota, or \\\\\"how close am I to my limits?\\\\\"\\\\n- A request to review Amazon EBS posture before a launch, migration or peak event.\\\\n\\\\nDo not use this skill for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, instance store, or Amazon EC2 issues unrelated to Amazon EBS.\\\\n\\\\n## Prerequisites\\\\n\\\\n- Read-only permissions for the APIs listed in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md).\\\\n- AWS CloudTrail access is optional. The skill works without it.\\\\n- Mutating changes run only through directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App), which need their own role and operator approval on the approval card.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nCopy this checklist and tick each step as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Load the shared references\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Run the path and draft the report\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Check the draft, fix it, then present it\\\\n\\\\n## Step 1: Classify the Request\\\\n\\\\n| The user says or the alarm shows | Mode and path | Load |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| \\\\\"My app is slow\\\\\", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics, `EBSIOBalance%` or `EBSByteBalance%`, \\\\\"is it storage?\\\\\", \\\\\"how much IOPS do I Report\\\\n\\\\nFollow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs. Then draft the report in the format below.\\\\n\\\\n### Troubleshoot verdict format\\\\n\\\\n1. **Answer:** the asked question, answered first.\\\\n2. **Evidence:** values with units and time window.\\\\n3. **Binding layer:** Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment (only with a direct signal, see [references/finding-logic.md](references/finding-logic.md)), Indeterminate, or Not applicable.\\\\n4. **Recommendation:** exact parameters, or \\\\\"No change\\\\\".\\\\n5. **Separate findings:** other true facts that do not change the Answer.\\\\n6. **Gaps:** what could not be checked and why.\\\\n\\\\nIn an investigation, put the Answer and the Recommendation with its exact parameters in the root cause finding, not only under Gaps. Keep the findings on the resource the user asked about. Mention another volume only when it shares the same instance EBS baseline, and then as a Separate finding.\\\\n\\\\nWhen the Binding layer is Indeterminate, report it as one finding. Do not offer AWS-side impairment as a hypothesis. List each direct check you ran (volume status, `VolumeStalledIOCheck`, AWS Health, AWS FIS) with its result as supporting evidence, say that no check confirms or rules out an EBS-side slowdown, and give the escalation path.\\\\n\\\\nReview mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md). Every Review mode response MUST begin with its Summary table, which rates all six areas (capacity and quota headroom, observability, cost hygiene, resilience, encryption posture, deletion protection), even when an area has no findings or is `Indeterminate`. The Summary table is required, not optional. Do not open with prose or an offer to run the review; start with the table, then the per-area detail.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Check the Draft Before Presenting It\\\\n\\\\nReview the draft from Step 3 against these checks. Fix anything that fails, then present it.\\\\n\\\\n- Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window, and matches the resource ID it is attributed to.\\\\n- The Binding layer agrees with the Evidence: the named layer is the one at its limit, and the other layers were checked and shown to have headroom. The Evidence gives the instance EBS baseline in MiB/s and IOPS next to the summed demand of all attached volumes.\\\\n- Any Recommendation stays within the instance\\'s EBS baseline and the volume type\\'s documented limits, and it is not more provisioning for an impairment.\\\\n- Every snapshot tier is backed by the checks it requires; if one of those checks failed, the item is not listed for owner review. No snapshot is recommended for deletion; the owner confirms first.\\\\n- A review answer starts with the Summary table and rates all six areas.\\\\n- Every API that failed or was not called is listed under Gaps.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Critical Rules\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App). Approval is given only on the approval card. A typed \\\\\"approve\\\\\" in chat is not approval.\\\\n- **Deletes are manual customer steps.** AWS DevOps Agent refuses delete-class operations (for example DeleteSnapshot, DeleteVolume, DeregisterImage), so never propose them as directed actions. After the owner confirms they no longer need the resource, give the commands for the customer to run with their own credentials.\\\\n- **Answer in one reply.** In chat, run the checks in this conversation and return the finished verdict or report as your reply. Do not hand the work to a background sub-agent and reply with a \\\\\"started\\\\\" or \\\\\"I will report back\\\\\" message, because that message becomes the answer the user sees first.\\\\n- **Discover, don\\'t assume:** read every configuration value from the APIs.\\\\n- **Rule EBS in or out before tuning it.**\\\\n- **Answer the asked question first;** other findings go under \\\\\"Separate findings\\\\\".\\\\n- **Review mode starts with the Summary table.** Every Review mode response begins with the Summary table of all six rated areas. The table is required, not optional.\\\\n- **Always check the instance layer** and size changes within the instance\\'s EBS **baseline**.\\\\n- **Never recommend more provisioning for an impairment.**\\\\n- **Use current service rules:** up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the most recent modification per volume; modification history and counts come from the optional AWS CloudTrail `ModifyVolume` events, or are listed under Gaps.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n\\\\n- A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.\\\\n- `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports EBS bandwidth in MB/s. Convert it to MiB/s before comparing it with volume throughput.\\\\n- On io1 and io2, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` is the percentage of provisioned IOPS delivered. It is not a throughput signal.\\\\n- `VolumeAvgIOPS`, `VolumeAvgThroughput`, `VolumeAvgReadLatency` and `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` need both `VolumeId` and `InstanceId` and exist only on Nitro instances. `VolumeAvgThroughput` is in KiB/s. `VolumeTotalReadTime` and `VolumeTotalWriteTime` are in seconds.\\\\n- Rising latency and queue length with falling IOPS is not proof of an AWS-side impairment. Without a direct signal (failed `VolumeStalledIOCheck`, impaired volume status, or an open AWS Health event) and without a running AWS FIS experiment, the Binding layer is Indeterminate.\\\\n- `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the latest modification per volume. It cannot count modifications in the last 24 hours.\\\\n- `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` without `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true also lists snapshots that AWS Backup did not create.\\\\n- A snapshot whose source volume is gone may be the only remaining copy of the data. List it for owner review; never call it safe to delete.\\\\n- Snapshots are incremental, so deleting one may free less storage than its size suggests.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nErrors, gated reads and missing metrics are handled with the fallback table in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). {"id": "c6753197-415e-4c93-ac48-5a1ac03a1a6c", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_e8R0BJRRWVu2K3Hmgfqej8", "content": "[{'text': '# Review mode: Amazon EBS operational review\\n\\nReview mode answers \"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\". It is entirely read-only. Run each area per Region, rate each finding with the scale in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md), and write the report with [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\nThe Capacity and quota headroom section is also a shared capability. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Find quotas by name; never hardcode codes. `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota` shows the default.\\n3. Compute usage from the inventory:\\n   - Provisioned IOPS: sum of `Iops` for io1 volumes and for io2 volumes, separately.\\n   - Storage per type: sum of `Size` per volume type, converted from GiB to TiB.\\n   - Snapshots per Region: count of `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self`.\\n   - Fast snapshot restore: `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores` count of enabled entries.\\n4. `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` for pending requests. Never propose a duplicate.\\n\\n**Rating rule**\\n\\n- Usage at or above 80% of the applied quota is flagged. The 80% value is this skill\\'s own heuristic, not an AWS rule or limit. It is configurable; ask the operator if they use a different one, and say in the report which value was used.\\n- A quota that blocked an operation is `High`.\\n- A quota flagged at or above the threshold is `Medium`, or `High` if the user states a planned increase that would exceed it.\\n- Unreadable quota or usage is `Indeterminate`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n- Adjustable: a pre-filled Service Quotas request (service code `ebs`, quota code as read, desired value) proposed as a directed action. The desired value is the user\\'s stated need, or current usage plus the request that failed. No fixed multipliers. Include the intake questions for the matching quota below, and show the adjustable-path approval caution.\\n- Not adjustable: draft the AWS Support case text (service, quota name, Region, desired value, business justification). Include the intake questions for the matching quota below, and show the case-path approval caution.\\n- Name the quotas that commonly cause problems: per-Region IOPS for io1 and io2, per-Region storage per volume type, snapshots per Region, and fast snapshot restore.\\n\\n**Suggested intake questions to include with the request or case**\\n\\nThese are this skill\\'s suggested questions, not an AWS requirement or form. Add the questions for the quota being proposed. The agent asks them in plain, customer-facing wording. Answering them in the request gives the reviewer more context about the need. Do not promise approval or a timeframe.\\n\\nThe archiving best practices are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/archiving-guidelines.html.\\n\\n**How to reason about archiving daily or weekly snapshots (guidance, not an AWS rule)**\\n\\nThere is no fixed change-rate threshold for archiving. Compare costs with the model in the archive documentation, using the current rates from the Amazon EBS pricing page. Do not type a price.\\n\\n1. What archiving saves: only the blocks of the snapshot that no other snapshot references leave the standard tier. Their size times the standard tier snapshot rate, for the time you keep the snapshot, is the saving. The archiving best practices page shows how the customer can count those blocks.\\n2. What archiving costs: the archived snapshot is a full snapshot (`FullSnapshotSizeInBytes` in `DescribeSnapshots`). Its size times the archive tier rate, for at least the 90-day minimum archive period, plus the restore charge per GB for each expected restore, plus standard tier storage while a restored copy is kept.\\n3. Archiving lowers cost only when step 1 is larger than step 2. The archiving best practices page shows that when later snapshots reference an archived snapshot\\'s data, the standard tier cost does not go down and the total cost goes up. Check the numbers for the customer\\'s snapshots instead of assuming.\\n\\nSources: snapshot archive (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-archive.html), pricing and billing for archiving (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-archive-pricing.html), archiving best practices (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/archiving-guidelines.html), Amazon EBS pricing (https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/).\\n\\n- IOPS or storage:\\n  - What workload is driving the need for more storage or IOPS? Is there a planned launch or event, or is this organic growth you want to secure capacity for?\\n  - How will the workload be spread across Availability Zones? If it is not spread evenly, which zone will carry most of the usage?\\n  - By what date do you need the extra capacity, and what is the ramp-up timeline?\\n  - What is the minimum amount you need?\\n- Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR):\\n  - What is your use case for a higher FSR limit?\\n  - How is this split across Availability Zones?\\n  - Will you enable FSR gradually in batches or all at once, and for how many snapshots?\\n  - What is the size of the snapshots you are enabling FSR on?\\n  - For how long will FSR stay enabled?\\n- Maximum number of archived snapshots per volume (include these only when the requested value is more than 25):\\n  - Is this for daily or weekly snapshots? If so, have you compared the archive cost with the standard tier saving, as described in the archiving reasoning above?\\n  - Is this for monthly, quarterly, or yearly snapshots? If so, why do you need more than 25 archived snapshots per volume?\\n  - Is this for new or existing snapshots? EBS Snapshots Archive stores full versions of snapshots. Have you reviewed the archiving best practices linked above?\\n- Maximum number of in-progress snapshot archives (include these only when the requested value is more than 25):\\n  - Is this for daily or weekly snapshots? If so, have you compared the archive cost with the standard tier saving, as described in the archiving reasoning above?\\n  - Is this for monthly, quarterly, or yearly snapshots?\\n  - Is this for new or existing snapshots? EBS Snapshots Archive stores full versions of snapshots. Have you reviewed the archiving best practices linked above?\\n  - Is this a one-time archival? Can you archive in batches of 25?\\n- Max concurrent copy-volume operations (volume clone):\\n  - What is the use case?\\n  - Which Availability Zones will you use in the Region?\\n  - What are the source and target volume types?\\n  - What is the estimated size of data on these volumes?\\n  - How often will you clone a volume (daily, weekly, or monthly)?\\n- Amazon EBS Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization:\\n  - Which Availability Zones will you use with this feature?\\n  - What snapshot sizes will you use?\\n  - Which volume types will you use?\\n  - How many volumes will you create at the same time with this feature?\\n  - How often will you create volumes with this feature (hourly, daily, or weekly)?\\n\\n**Approval caution (always show with the request or case)**\\n\\n- Adjustable path (show with the pre-filled Service Quotas request): A request through Service Quotas is not guaranteed. AWS reviews each one and may approve a lower value than you asked for or ask for more detail, and a very large increase may be routed to AWS Support before it is granted.\\n- Case path (show with the AWS Support case text): Approval and the exact amount are decided by AWS.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EBS namespace: alarms on `VolumeQueueLength`, latency (`VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency`, or `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeTotalWriteTime` math), throughput, and `BurstBalance` for gp2, st1 and sc1.\\n2. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EC2 namespace: `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on instances that publish them.\\n3. Which volumes are critical: ask the operator, or use tags they name. Do not infer criticality from tag values by yourself.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical volume with no Amazon EBS alarm is `Medium`. `High` if the operator says the volume backs a production database or service.
